paragraphs: A rich man owned a garden and employed two gardeners. One of them was lazy and hardly worked at all. But whenever the owner visited, this gardener would jump up, fold his hands, praise how beautiful his master's face was, and dance in front of him.
The other gardener said very little. He simply worked hard, raised all kinds of fruit and vegetables, and carried them on his head all the way to his master, who lived far away.
Which of the two, Swamiji asked, would the master love more?

Shiva, he explained, is that master, and this world is His garden. Here too there are two kinds of gardeners. One is lazy and insincere, doing nothing but going on about Shiva's beautiful eyes and features. The other looks after Shiva's children: the poor, the weak, the animals, all of creation.

Of course Shiva loves the second one more. If you want to serve the father, serve his children first. Whoever wants to serve Shiva must first serve every creature in this world. The scriptures say that those who serve God's servants are His greatest servants, and Swamiji asked his listeners to remember this.
learn: Devotion isn't measured by how loudly you praise, but by how much you care for others. Helping someone who is struggling, tutoring a junior, feeding an animal: that is worship in action.
